title: させてもらう: receiving a caused action
summary: The causative (cause someone to do) plus もらう (receive) gives させてもらう: "receive being caused to", often a polite way to ask or to announce.

blocks.text: させてもらう looks scary, but it is built from two pieces you already know. The **causative** せる / させる means **cause** someone to do something (lesson 19), and **もらう** receives an action (lesson 49). Put them together and you get "receive someone's causing".
The causative means cause, not only make or allow

English splits "make" from "let", but the Japanese causative covers any way of causing. Even English cheats on this: "I'll **let** you know tomorrow" does not mean "allow" or "force". It means "cause you to know". Japanese says it with the causative of 知る: **知らせる**. In the same way, **聞かせる** is "cause to hear", and 読み聞かせる is to read aloud to someone.

Make the causative て-form and add もらう. 聞かせてもらえますか is "may I receive your causing me to hear?", that is "could you tell me?" The doer takes に, as usual with もらう. The one being caused is not always you: メガネを合わせてもらった means "I received the glasses being caused to fit", that is, "I had my glasses fitted".
先生に聞かせてもらった。 (I) was told by the teacher. (lit. received the teacher causing me to hear)

帰らせてもらいます means "I will receive your allowing me to go home", close to English "with your permission, I'll go home now". Whether it is truly polite or a thin polite wrapper depends on tone. The humble verb **いただく** replaces もらう in very polite speech: 帰らせていただきます. It means the same thing and adds humility.

blocks.jp: ちょっと考えさせてもらえますか。
blocks.en: Could you let me think about it for a moment?

blocks.jp: 明日、早く帰らせてもらいます。
blocks.en: (With your leave) I'll head home early tomorrow.

blocks.jp: 説明を聞かせてもらえませんか。
blocks.en: Could you tell me the explanation?

items: The causative means **cause**, which covers make, allow and arrange.
**Vさせてもらう** = receive someone's causing (me) to V.
**〜てもらえますか / もらえませんか** asks politely: can I receive …?
**いただく** is the humble form of もらう.

questions.instruction: Which verb means "cause someone to know"?

questions.note: 休ま + せて + もらう.

questions.instruction: What does 聞かせてもらえますか ask?
options: May I ask you to leave?
questions.note: Receive your causing me to hear.

questions.instruction: Which is the humble form of もらう?
questions.note: いただきます literally "I humbly receive".
It means cause, which includes allow and arrange.

questions.instruction: Which sentence means "I'll go home now (with your leave)"?
questions.note: 帰らせて + もらいます.
言わせてもらった carries the whole receive-caused-saying chain.

questions.instruction: In メガネを合わせてもらった, who is caused to fit?
questions.note: The glasses are made to fit; I receive that.

questions.instruction: Which particle marks the person who does the causing?
questions.note: As with もらう in general.

questions.note: The amount comes first, then the causative て-form, then もらえますか.

questions.instruction: What does 読み聞かせる describe?
questions.note: 読み + 聞かせる: read and cause to hear.
